 PlayStation 5 Pro Prices Go Absolutely Wild Ahead Of GTA 6 Release
 By   Marcus Mears III 
 Nov. 18, 2026 7:17 am EST 
 Miguel Lagoa/Shutterstock

 We may receive a commission on purchases made from links. 
 PlayStation 5 Pro prices have been rising steadily over the last few years due to the ongoing memory shortage brought on by AI datacenters. Throw Grand Theft Auto VI into the mix, one of the most anticipated game releases of all time, and prices for Sony's console have gotten completely out of control. According to the MSRP on the PlayStation Direct store , the PlayStation 5 Pro is supposed to cost $899, but stock is listed as "Currently Unavailable" and the chance of you finding a console anywhere near that price is virtually zero.
 Grand Theft Auto VI is set to launch on November 19th as a console exclusive title. Many players have been waiting well over a decade for GTA VI, ever since Grand Theft Auto V's release in 2013 and are now jumping at the chance to play it as soon as possible, which means buying a PS5 Pro — the console Rockstar has stated will make Grand Theft Auto VI look the best — or an Xbox Series X, which isn't as performant and can still cost well over $1,000.
 You might also think to check retailers like Amazon, Best Buy, and Walmart for PlayStation 5 Pro availability. And while you can find some PS5 Pro consoles in stock, asking prices are over double that of the MSRP and typically fulfilled by third-party suppliers with longer shipping times. Best Buy's cheapest PS5 Pro is $1,994.99 , with listings all the way up to $1,899.99 completely sold out. The story at Amazon is largely the same, with used and renewed listings reaching well over $1,500, and the cheapest new PS5 Pro listed for $1,794.99 . 
 Are there any cheap PlayStation 5 Pro consoles left?
 Vitaliy Potapov1/Shutterstock 
 Prices for the PlayStation 5 Pro are unlikely to see a meaningful correction anytime soon. Outside of the hype of the GTA VI release, memory shortages for components like RAM and SSDs are driving an industry-wide price increase for businesses and consumers alike across PC and console. With that said, there are a few methods to potentially land a PS5 Pro at a cheaper price than nearly $2,000.
 The first way is the simplest: set a price alert at retailers like Best Buy so you can get a notification as soon as a PS5 Pro goes on sale. Just know that thousands of other prospective players — and scalpers — already have these set up, so you have to be particularly quick on the draw if you want to take advantage of a discount.
 The next route is to look for a second-hand console at services like eBay and Facebook Marketplace. There are actually a decent number of pre-owned consoles listed for around $1,200 to $1,500 at eBay. This method comes with its own pitfalls though — eBay does have a money-back guarantee policy if the item you received is broken or doesn't match the description, but you have to be vigilant when it comes to recognizing scams and "Box only" listings. Make sure to read the description, look at the photos, and check the seller's reviews before committing to a purchase.
 PlayStation is too expensive -- what about PC and Xbox?
 LarysaP/Shutterstock 
 Unfortunately, prebuilt PCs and PC component prices are largely affected by the memory shortage as well. Even budget-level Nvidia GPUs aren't really affordable  anymore, and AMD Radeon cards have recently fallen victim to the same steep price increases. Building a PC equivalent to the PS5 Pro would still cost about $1,500, with 16GB of DDR5 memory costing $250 on its own. You will also have to wait until the title gets ported to PC because GTA VI is slated to release as a console exclusive. Rockstar hasn't given an official statement on the release date for PC, but some analysts have suggested a Q1 2027 release looks promising.
 Xbox Series X and S owners can play Rockstar's latest release on day one too, though the hardware doesn't stack up to the PS5 Pro. GTA VI is capped at 30FPS on consoles because its level of storyline detail and impressive visual fidelity are extremely taxing, and the Xbox Series X|S may struggle at higher settings in more resource-intensive scenes. 
 Amazon currently has next to no availability for the Xbox Series X.  Best Buy has a 1TB Xbox Series X for $1,089 from a third-party seller as well as several bundles around the $1,200 to $1,500 price range. Rockstar also announced that Xbox One owners will be able to play GTA VI through Xbox Cloud Gaming .
